security_justification.audit_integrity: Generated assessment artifacts preserve all required governance assertions and audit trail records without omission.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: Does not modify, bypass, or interact with any authentication or authorization mechanisms.
security_justification.authority_provenance: Derives public change metadata only; no cryptographic signing or identity authority logic is altered.
security_justification.concurrency: Purely synchronous file I/O operations with no shared memory, concurrent workers, or race conditions.
security_justification.confidentiality: Operates solely on public change planning metadata and repository commit hashes; handles no sensitive data.
security_justification.cryptography: Does not introduce, alter, or rely upon cryptographic operations or secret management.
security_justification.error_disclosure: Reports descriptive file diff and schema mismatch diagnostics without disclosing system secrets or credentials.
security_justification.external_security_integration: Operates independently without external network connections, APIs, or third-party security services.
security_justification.fail_posture: Fails closed upon syntax errors, missing source files, invalid schema structures, or byte-for-byte drift.
security_justification.lifecycle: Bounded to one-shot CLI execution during change planning or CI verification phases.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: Emits assessment artifacts strictly within the targeted change directory; enforces read-only verification in check mode.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: Does not process user telemetry, personal data, or sensitive operational payloads.
security_justification.resource_retention: Retains no in-memory buffers, persistent file handles, or network sockets beyond script termination.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: Deterministic idempotency; re-running generator produces identical bytes with no side effects.
security_justification.trust_boundary: Tool operates strictly within local developer and CI environments; modifies no trust boundary or security perimeter.
